name: hcapp_saveHashTrash
description: Creates or updates the HashTrash article for a run. HashTrash is a headline + markdown article written per run by mismanagement. Status 0 = draft (mismanagement only); 1 = published (visible to all). Only the three HashTrash columns on HC.Event are touched — updatedAt is deliberately NOT updated so that the sync pipeline does not re-distribute the event row to all clients. Auth: HC6.ValidateAppAuth (spNumber 53, @param NULL — device-secret token). Permission gate: HC6.CheckKennelPermission @functionKey = 'writeHashTrash' in @kennelId (Hash Flash 0x20, WebMeister 0x1000 or GM 0x02 — bitmask 0x1022; see /hc-authorizations). Write SP: two-rowset error shape ({success=0, errorCode, errorType} then the error detail) or the single success envelope. New feature — no HC5 equivalent.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: Registered device UUID. Passed to HC6.ValidateAppAuth for auth resolution. No SQL default.

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Short-lived auth token validated against DeviceSecret. No SQL default.

parameters.name: kennelId
parameters.description: Kennel that owns the event; also the scope of the permission check. Required — NULL or zero-UUID returns errorCode 1234, errorType 2. No SQL default.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: Event to write HashTrash for. Required — NULL or zero-UUID returns errorCode 1234, errorType 2. If no non-deleted event matches eventId + kennelId, returns errorCode 4040, errorType 3. No SQL default.

parameters.name: headline
parameters.description: Short article headline. Required — NULL, empty or whitespace-only returns errorCode 1234, errorType 2. No SQL default. Event.HashTrashHeadline is not in db/schema/tables/HC.Event.Table.sql (added by a later migration); its width could not be checked against the parameter.
parameters.typeMismatch: Column definition not in db/schema/tables — width unverified. The NVARCHAR(500) parameter silently truncates longer user text (see codeSmells).

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: Markdown body of the article. The body tolerates NULL or empty (validation only requires @headline), but the parameter has NO SQL default, so a client must send it — omitting it is an unlogged 500. Column not in db/schema/tables (see @headline).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: 0 = draft (mismanagement-only visibility); 1 = published (all users). Any other value — including NULL, since NULL NOT IN (0, 1) is UNKNOWN and the IF fires — returns errorCode 1234, errorType 2. No SQL default. Column not in db/schema/tables (see @headline).

rowsets.name: ErrorEnvelope
rowsets.description: Compact error envelope returned on auth failure (ValidateAppAuth codes), validation (1234 / type 2), permission (1334 / type 3), event-not-found (4040 / type 3) or unhandled error (1933 / type 5): { success=0, errorCode, errorType }. Followed by StandardErrorResult at index 1. Mutually exclusive with SuccessEnvelope.

rowsets.name: SuccessEnvelope
rowsets.description: Returned on successful save: { success=1, errorCode=NULL, errorType=NULL }. The only rowset on success. Mutually exclusive with ErrorEnvelope.
Returned at index 1 alongside the ErrorEnvelope (index 0) on any error. Columns: errorId, errorType, errorCode, errorTitle, errorUserMessage, errorProc (no debugMessage).

sideEffects: UPDATE HC.Event SET HashTrashHeadline, HashTrashContent, HashTrashStatus WHERE id = @eventId AND KennelId = @kennelId AND deleted = 0. Deliberately does NOT touch updatedAt, so the row is not re-synced to devices.
INSERT HC.ErrorLog on validation (1234), permission (1334), event-not-found (4040) and unhandled (1933) errors; ValidateAppAuth logs its own auth failures.

codeSmells.detail: These parameters have no SQL default, so a call that omits one is refused by SQL Server before the procedure runs (unlogged empty 500): @deviceId, @accessToken, @content, @status. On 2026-10-13 every parameter whose body already handled NULL (and every sync watermark) was given a default; these remain because they are the auth pair or the body never checks them for NULL.

Line 7: @headline NVARCHAR(500) is typed by a hasher. SQL Server silently truncates a parameter to its declared width — no error, no HC.ErrorLog row, a headline that just ends. There is no LEN() check against the column width and no error envelope for 'too long'. Declare NVARCHAR(MAX), check LEN() against Event.HashTrashHeadline's width and return the 1234 envelope; cap the client at the same number.

codeSmells.issue: Intentional updatedAt omission bypasses sync — HashTrash must be fetched on demand
codeSmells.detail: Lines 112-118 update the three HashTrash columns without updatedAt, by design, so the event row is not redistributed to every device. Consequence for callers: after a save the local synced Event row does NOT carry the new article; HashTrash is read through its own SP, never from local sync data.

breakingChanges: 1.1.0 (2026-10-13): contract corrections only — @content marked non-nullable (no SQL default), envelope success typed INT, auth/permission gate and error codes documented.
